# Results — Study 834 (Minimum Backtest Length / MinTRL)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py) on a **deterministic, offline synthetic
world** (base seed 834, `ann_vol = 0.15`). This is a research-method demonstration of Bailey,
Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (2014): given a target annualised Sharpe there is a **minimum
track-record length** below which you cannot reject "true Sharpe ≤ 0" at 95% — so a short backtest
cannot tell skill from luck. Real free data can never certify "true Sharpe = 0", so there is no
real-tape stamp; the limitation is named on the Signal axis and the study is capped at `NONE`. Run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**. Fingerprint
`c648fb3ad2b5` (sim config: seed 834, daily freq 252, conf 0.95, ann-vol 0.15, 4,000 sims).*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Do short backtests fail to tell skill from luck?" `CONFIRMED`

The Sharpe ratio you read off a backtest is a **noisy estimate** of the true one, and the noise
scales with `1/√(track length)`. Bailey–Borwein–López de Prado–Zhu turn that into a hard number: the
**Minimum Track Record Length (MinTRL)** — the shortest history over which an observed Sharpe of a
given size becomes statistically significant at a chosen confidence. Its companion is the
**Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (PSR)**, the probability the true Sharpe beats a benchmark given the
observed Sharpe, the sample moments, and the length. In observations,

```
MinTRL_obs = 1 + [ 1 - skew·sr + (kurt-1)/4·sr² ] · ( Z_conf / (sr - sr*) )²
```

with `sr = SR_ann/√freq` the per-observation Sharpe and `Z_conf = Φ⁻¹(conf)`. For Gaussian daily
returns this collapses to the rule of thumb **MinTRL_years ≈ (Z_conf/SR_ann)²**.

- `NONE` on the Signal axis — a synthetic-only method demo on a world we *built* to have zero edge;
  there is no real Sharpe to detect, and the only pretty backtest is luck.
- `MIRAGE` on Tradability — a backtest shorter than its MinTRL is statistically indistinguishable
  from a coin flip, so there is nothing to harvest and costs are moot.
- `CONFIRMED` on the myth-check — the pitfall is real and material: the required length grows as
  `(Z/SR)²` (10.8 yr at Sharpe 0.5, **43 yr** at Sharpe 0.25), the null false-positive rate is
  calibrated at its nominal 5%, and even a *genuine* Sharpe-1 strategy is only ~50% detectable at its
  2.71-year MinTRL.

## The headline — MinTRL (years) vs annualised Sharpe (Gaussian daily, 95% one-sided)

| target Sharpe | MinTRL (exact) | rule of thumb `(Z/SR)²` |
|---|--:|--:|
| **2.00** | **0.69 yr** | 0.68 yr |
| **1.00** | **2.71 yr** | 2.71 yr |
| **0.50** | **10.83 yr** | 10.82 yr |
| **0.25** | **43.30 yr** | 43.29 yr |

The required history **explodes as the Sharpe falls** (quadratically): halving the target Sharpe
*quadruples* the track record you need. Most published strategies quote a Sharpe of 0.3–0.7 on a
5–10 year backtest — comfortably *inside* their MinTRL, i.e. too short to distinguish from luck.

## Negative skew and fat tails lengthen the requirement (monthly returns, Sharpe 1.0, 95%)

The `[1 - skew·sr + (kurt-1)/4·sr²]` factor bites hardest at the monthly reporting frequency where
`sr` per observation is largest — the realistic hedge-fund setting.

| return shape | MinTRL | vs Gaussian |
|---|--:|--:|
| Gaussian (skew 0, kurt 3) | **2.90 yr** | ×1.00 |
| skew −1, kurt 4.5 | **3.77 yr** | ×1.30 |
| skew −2, kurt 9 (fat left tail) | **4.80 yr** | ×1.65 |

A negatively-skewed, fat-tailed track record — exactly the profile of a strategy that sells tail risk
(steady gains, occasional crashes) — needs **two-thirds longer** before its Sharpe is trustworthy.
The naive `(Z/SR)²` rule *understates* the requirement for the very strategies most prone to blow up.

## The pitfall — short backtests cannot tell skill from luck (worthless world, true Sharpe 0)

4,000 backtests of a **driftless** series (true annualised Sharpe = 0):

| window | fraction posting observed Sharpe ≥ 1.0 | best backtest seen |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1 year | **15.6 %** | Sharpe **3.40** |
| 2 years | **8.4 %** | Sharpe **2.45** |

The observed Sharpe of a *worthless* 2-year backtest has a standard deviation of **0.72** around zero
— so roughly 1 in 12 worthless strategies posts a headline Sharpe above 1.0, and the luckiest looks
*spectacular*. This is the whole game: with enough short backtests, a gaudy Sharpe is guaranteed
somewhere, with no skill involved.

## Calibration — the PSR test is unbiased on the null (should reject ~5%)

The correction is not a fudge: on the null (true Sharpe 0), the PSR(0) ≥ 0.95 test fires at exactly
its nominal false-positive rate, at every track length.

| window | PSR(0) ≥ 0.95 fires | Wilson 95% band | nominal |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 year | **5.60 %** | 4.93–6.36 % | 5.00 % |
| 2 years | **5.65 %** | 4.98–6.41 % | 5.00 % |
| 5 years | **5.27 %** | 4.62–6.01 % | 5.00 % |

The machinery is honest: it does *not* over-reject on the null (that would manufacture false edges),
and it does *not* under-reject (that would hide real ones). *(A faithful-engine check — never cited in
support of a real-tape stamp; there is no real tape here.)*

## Positive control — a genuine Sharpe-1 strategy is only confirmable past its length

The same machinery on a world with a **real** annualised Sharpe of 1.0. MinTRL(SR=1) = **2.71 yr** is
where an observed-equals-target Sharpe *becomes significant* (~50% of true draws clear it); reliably
*detecting* the edge (95% power) needs the longer **10.82 yr**.

| track length | detected (PSR ≥ 0.95) | Wilson 95% band |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1.00 yr | **25.3 %** | 24.0–26.7 % |
| 2.71 yr (MinTRL) | **50.0 %** | 48.5–51.5 % |
| 5.00 yr | **70.8 %** | 69.4–72.2 % |
| 10.82 yr (95%-power) | **95.0 %** | 94.3–95.6 % |

Genuine edge *is* eventually confirmable — but a 1–2 year track record misses a real Sharpe-1
strategy three times out of four. Short backtests are underpowered in *both* directions: they cry wolf
on the worthless and stay silent on the skilful.

## Why the verdict is what it is

1. **Nothing real to find.** The world is built to have zero edge; the only gaudy Sharpe is luck, and
   a synthetic-only demo can never earn `REAL` (which needs a robust *t* ≥ 2 on a real tape).
   **Signal `NONE`.**
2. **Nothing to trade.** A backtest shorter than its MinTRL is statistically a coin flip; there is no
   harvestable edge and costs never enter. **Tradability `MIRAGE`.**
3. **The pitfall is real and quantified.** The required length grows as `(Z/SR)²` — 43 years at
   Sharpe 0.25 — is inflated further by negative skew and fat tails, the null test is calibrated at
   5%, and even a true Sharpe-1 is a coin flip at its MinTRL. **`CONFIRMED`.**

## The honest takeaway

A Sharpe ratio without its track-record length is meaningless. Before you believe a backtest, compute
its MinTRL: if the history is shorter than `(Z/SR)²` years, the number cannot be distinguished from
luck — and if the returns are negatively skewed and fat-tailed (they usually are), the bar is higher
still. `NONE` × `MIRAGE`, pitfall `CONFIRMED`. This is a method demo on a synthetic world by design.
